observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a compression-testing rig: a large polished cylindrical steel platen sits on top of a horizontal stack of pale wooden sticks bound in clear plastic film, which in turn rests on a yellow-and-black diagonally striped cylindrical base. The background is a flat pale grey-green machine frame, with a vertical yellow-and-black striped guide rail fixed at the left edge. The base, frame, and left rail stay in the same image position throughout, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The upper steel platen descends gradually relative to the wood stack and the static base across the segment (its lower edge moves from roughly the top of the uppermost stick early on to noticeably lower by the last frame).
The plastic-wrapped stack of wooden sticks is progressively compressed: its overall height shrinks between the first and last frames while its bottom edge remains on the base.
As the stack shortens, a splintered stick end protrudes more prominently at the upper-right side of the stack (small/absent early, more visible in later frames).
The clear plastic wrap creases and shifts slightly with the compression but remains around the stack.
outside_clip_unknowns: The applied force/load values and the machine's control settings are not visible.
Whether the platen's descent started before this segment or continues after it is unknown; both endpoints are arbitrary crop boundaries.
The final outcome of the test (full crushing, rebound, or release) is not shown.
uncertain_details: The exact amount of compression cannot be quantified from the frames.
It is unclear whether the right-side protrusion is a newly broken splinter or simply a stick end revealed by the shifting stack.
Minor apparent vertical shifts of the whole assembly are hard to separate from the platen's true downward motion, though the fixed base and left rail argue the camera is static.
